facts.text: An edge case lies at the limit of one parameter, a corner case lies at the limits of several parameters simultaneously, and a rare event occurs so seldom in normal operation that waiting for it is not a practical testing method.
facts.quote: An edge case sits at the limit of one parameter, a corner case sits at the limits of several at once, and a rare event is a situation that happens so seldom in normal operation that waiting for it is not a practical way to test it.

facts.text: Systems that work well away from parameter limits often fail in corner cases, motivating failure-seeking tests at those limits.
facts.quote: Systems that work well in the middle often fail in the corners, which is why test engineers hunt there.

facts.text: A worker stepping out from behind a parked truck exactly as a loader starts reversing is a rare event and a fatal accident pattern.
facts.quote: A worker who steps out from behind a parked truck exactly as a loader starts to reverse is rare, and it is also the accident pattern that kills.

facts.text: Demonstrating a miss rate of at most 1% with zero observed misses requires 299 independent trials.

facts.text: The "curse of rarity" (2024) explains why the tail becomes harder to test as the number of variables grows.
